result.strongest_objection: The doc's headline premise — 'no behaviour change on any failure path (§3)' in the Item line, reinforced by §3.3's table claiming 'identical' failure semantics on every path — is falsified by the doc's own §6 R1. Before the hoist, a foreign process dialing a profile's net6 between bind and control() had a ~microsecond window (bind and control() are adjacent at HEAD); after the hoist that window equals the profile's entire pre-bind work (randomHex, two Mkdirs, NewExecHandler, plus ~8.5–14 ms of measured Git for protected profiles, V9). A foreign accept inside that widened window now makes control() observe 2 accepts and refuse startup ('accept count 2 after one connect, want 1') — a failure-path outcome that is unreachable-in-practice at HEAD but reachable after the hoist. There exist executions that pass at HEAD and refuse after the hoist: that is a behaviour change on a failure path, on a fail-closed startup gate, and it is asserted away rather than measured (the foreign-dial rate is explicitly UNMEASURED, on a rig that had a live ailang-worldd running, V13). The refusal is fail-closed and never a false pass, so the design may still be right — but the premise as written is false, and §3.3's table omits the one row that would show it.
result.catch: Reconcile the Item bullet and §3.3 with §6 R1: either (a) scope the equivalence claim to in-process behavior and add the missing §3.3 row for the cross-process control-leg window, or (b) actually measure it. Separately, V9's 'real preflight Git latency' was measured with a failing `git config --get-regexp '^filter\.'` in a NON-repo dir (rc=1); the doc never quotes the actual command protectedGitPreflight runs or measures it inside a real worktree, so the '§1 row 4: ~20× margin' verdict rests on an unverified proxy — re-measure the real preflight in a populated repo or downgrade the claim.
result.proposed_fix: 1) Rewrite the Item claim to: 'Production +23/−18 lines. No in-process behaviour change on any failure path (§3.3); one cross-process failure window widens (§6 R1): a foreign accept landing between the hoisted bind and its owner's control() now produces a fail-closed refusal where HEAD's ~µs bind→control() adjacency made it practically unreachable. It cannot produce a false pass.' 2) Add a §3.3 table row: 'Foreign accept before control() | pass (window ≈ µs) | fail-closed refusal, error text unchanged (window = pre-bind work, incl. measured 8.5–14 ms protected Git, V9) — refuse-closed, never false-pass'. 3) Add a verification-log row that turns R1's UNMEASURED into measured: on the prototype, use the existing cfg.reversePort snapshot to obtain profile k's net6 port and dial it once before that profile's Run A; assert the resulting ExecProbeError is the arm6-network control-leg refusal exactly as HEAD would phrase it, and assert T1/T2 stay green; plus a baseline foreign-dial rate observation against the live daemon (V13) or an explicit UNMEASURED with rationale. 4) Correct §3.1 to 'Go ≥1.22 loop semantics (go.mod 1.26)'. 5) Re-run V9 inside a real profile worktree quoting the exact protectedGitPreflight invocation, or relabel the 20× margin as proxy-derived.
